title: Write an Ingress With TLS
intro: tutorial-010 had you reading an existing Ingress. Now write one that routes shop.example.com over HTTPS to the 'web' Service.

steps.prompt: Write an Ingress named 'web-ing' with ingressClassName: nginx. It routes host shop.example.com, path / (pathType: Prefix), to Service 'web' on port number 80. Add a tls section for shop.example.com using the secret 'shop-tls'.
steps.hint: Nesting is the hard part: spec.rules[] → host + http.paths[] → path, pathType, backend.service.{name, port.number}. TLS is a separate list: spec.tls[] → hosts (a list) + secretName. apiVersion is networking.k8s.io/v1.
steps.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web-ing
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - shop.example.com
    secretName: shop-tls
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: web
            port:
              number: 80
steps.explanation: External HTTPS traffic for shop.example.com is now terminated at the ingress controller and forwarded to the web Service.
steps.why: The TLS secret must contain a certificate whose SANs include shop.example.com (see networking-tutorial-007) — in practice cert-manager creates and renews it automatically from an annotation. Also note TLS terminates at the ingress: the app receives plain HTTP, which is exactly the setup that causes networking-incident-006's redirect loop if the app isn't told to trust X-Forwarded-Proto.
